Riding light (first light to last light, Vancouver): Sun, Nov 8 7:37am to 6:14pm; Mon, Nov 9 7:39am to 6:13pm; Tue, Nov 10 7:40am to 6:12pm. Hours outside that are dark and not listed; never suggest riding then.

Guillermo's own take for Sun, Nov 8 (his read, quote it as his, not yours): Howe Sound is way ahead of the page this morning. At 6:53am the Spit was SSE 28 gusting 37 (page about 16), and Pam Rocks read SSE 25 at 6am. Pemberton sits 5 hPa below Vancouver, so the inflow should keep pulling.

My pick is Squamish from first light (about 7:45am) into early afternoon, SSE 25 to 29 with gusts near 38. Small kites, experienced riders only. Check before driving: if the Spit still reads 20 or more at 9am, go.

Porteau is the backup until about 11:30, before the flood kills the swell. The Strait is softer than shown, Sand Heads only S 16.

Rider weed reports (floating weed or eelgrass, last 3 days; mention them when suggesting these spots): Tsawwassen Ferry Terminal Causeway: lots of weed (Fri, Nov 6 12:00).

EC marine forecast, Howe Sound (issued 04:00 AM PCT 08 November 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Today Tonight and Monday. Gale warning in effect. Wind southerly inflow 30 to 40 knots with gusts to 50 diminishing to southerly inflow 20 to 30 this morning with gusts to 35 ending early this afternoon. Wind diminishing to southerly inflow 10 to 20 late this afternoon then becoming northerly outflow 10 to 20 this evening. Wind increasing to northerly outflow 20 to 30 after midnight then diminishing to northerly outflow 10 to 20 near noon Monday.

Wind southerly 25 to 35 knots with gusts to 45 becoming south 20 to 30 this morning with gusts to 35 and veering to southwest 15 to 25 early this afternoon. Wind veering to southwest 15 to 20 Monday evening.
